title: Establish and Maintain Redwood-Verified Performance Profiles for Onboarded Models
creator: Meera Srinivasan
description: We need a repeatable, auditable process to publish and keep up-to-date Redwood-verified performance profiles for every model and model-version we onboard. Each profile must include latency (p50/p95/p99 by sequence length and batch size), throughput (tokens/sec at target batch sizes), and cost estimates (per-token cost given quantization/runtime config). Profiles must be generated by an automated benchmarking pipeline, stored as versioned artifacts, surfaced in the Model Catalog UI, and wired into version pinning and rollout controls. This ticket drives the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for a maintainable profile publishing system.
acceptance_criteria: Automated benchmarking pipeline that executes canonical workloads for a new model/version and produces a machine-readable performance profile JSON
Performance profiles are stored as immutable versioned artifacts (S3/GCS) with provenance (commit, runtime config, hardware, date)
Model Catalog UI displays the latest verified profile and a history view for pinned versions
Onboarding flow requires a verified profile before marking a model as supported in the hosted catalog (can be waived by PM with audit log)
Alerting for regression: nightly/per-week benchmarks detect >15% latency regression or >20% throughput drop vs pinned baseline and create ENG ticket automatically
Documentation (internal Confluence + public catalog blurb) explains methodology, CI settings, and cost model assumptions
tasks: Draft benchmark suite: canonical prompts for chat/completion/embedding, target sequence-length buckets, and cold vs hot-cache scenarios
Spec performance profile schema (fields: model, version, runtime_config, hardware, p50/p95/p99 latency arrays, throughput table, cost_estimates, provenance)
Implement benchmark runner in infra repo (ENG-2041) with reproducible environment + seed control
Add storage + immutability layer for artifacts and tagging convention
Expose profile metadata in onboarding UI and Model Catalog page (DES-324) with ‘verified’ badge
Integrate with version pinning: when customer pins a model, UI shows which verified profile is pinned
Create nightly regression job and alerting playbook; auto-create ENG ticket with perf-diff report
Author public-facing catalog guidance and internal playbook for re-benchmarking cadence (monthly/critical-release)
Define rollback policy and automatic fallback selection for runtime if a deployed model exceeds latency SLOs
risks: Hardware and region variability may make single-profile numbers misleading unless provenance is clear
Model nondeterminism and runtime changes can cause noisy comparisons; need statistical significance in regression detection
Running exhaustive benchmarks is costly; must balance coverage vs cost by sampling representative configs
Customers may expect guarantees from 'verified' wording; ensure we document scope and drift window clearly
Edge cases: private/dedicated deployments may have different performance characteristics — clarify scope of 'Redwood-verified' (hosted & validated dedicated configs only)
